title: Wasting Away in Grief
note: She can’t bear the parting. Thinking always of the pain she suffers, she wastes away and grieves.

couplets.plain: I would hide this sickness, but it rises like spring water for those who draw it.
couplets.pm: Ashamed that others should know, I hide this sickness. But it won’t stay hidden. It rises as spring water rises for those who draw it because they need it. So what use is hiding? Now you must do what comes next.
couplets.context: Her friend says that showing the sickness of desire doesn’t suit her sense of shame. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Hiding the sickness only raises it, as drawing from a spring brings up more water.

couplets.plain: I can’t hide this sickness, and telling the one who caused it brings me shame.
couplets.pm: I can’t hide this sickness from the people here, because it grows hour by hour. Telling the one who caused it brings shame too, because a message to one gone far would say that I am still alive. What am I to do?
couplets.context: Her friend says she must do one of two things: hide it from the people here, or send word to him. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: telling the one who caused it brings me shame

couplets.plain: Desire and shame hang from my life as from a carrying pole, inside this body that can’t bear them.
couplets.pm: The sickness of desire, and the shame that won’t let me tell him, hang in my failing body from the two ends of my life, as from a carrying pole. They balance exactly. One urges her to send word and the other forbids it, and together they are breaking her life. She can’t settle on either, so it will snap.
couplets.context: She goes on, answering her friend.
couplets.speaker: she
couplets.sensitive: Pictures the body breaking under grief.

links.quote: Desire and shame hang from my life
Desire and shame hang from my life
links.reason: The load at the other end, weighing as heavily as her desire.

couplets.plain: There is indeed a sea of desire. There is no safe raft to cross it.
couplets.pm: Of the two things that everyone may have, what I have is the sea of desire. The safe raft to cross it, I don’t have. The point is that you should have been that raft by sending word, and you haven’t.
couplets.context: Her friend says women like her don’t fall into the sea of desire, and if they do they cross it on a fitting raft. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Her desire lies before her as a sea to be crossed.

links.quote: no safe raft to cross it
links.reason: No safe raft exists to carry her over it.

couplets.plain: Those who can bring suffering even in friendship, what would they do in enmity?
couplets.pm: Those able to bring suffering into friendship, which should give joy, what would they do in enmity, which is meant to give pain? We have never seen them as enemies, so we can’t know. She is hurt that her friend doesn’t stop the suffering, so she blames her for it and speaks of her as someone else.
couplets.context: Hurt that no word has been sent to him, she says this to her friend.
couplets.speaker: she

couplets.plain: The joy of desire is a sea. But when it turns on you, the pain is greater than that sea.
couplets.pm: When desire gives joy through union, that joy is as great as the sea. When the same desire gives pain through parting, the pain is greater than the sea. If it only matched the joy received it could be borne, but it doesn’t.
couplets.context: Her friend says those who have had joy from desire will have pain from it too. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: The joy of desire is a sea
links.reason: Gives desire its two measures: joy as wide as the sea, and pain greater still.

links.quote: the pain is greater than that sea
links.reason: The sea is the measure of desire’s joy, and its pain goes past even that.

couplets.plain: I swim the fierce flood of desire and see no shore. Even at midnight I alone am here.
couplets.pm: I have swum the sea of desire, yet I find no shore. In the dead of night, when everyone sleeps, I am alone with no companion. And I don’t die and escape, but stay alive. What a fruit of evil deeds this is! “Alone” hints that you have been no companion to me.
couplets.context: Her friend says the sea of desire can be crossed with self-control as the raft. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: I swim the fierce flood of desire
links.reason: She swims the fierce flood of desire with no shore in sight.

links.quote: Even at midnight I alone am here

couplets.plain: Poor night. It has put all living things to sleep and has no companion but me.
couplets.pm: This night is a poor thing. It has itself put all the world’s living things to sleep, and so has no companion but me. It lets go all who could keep it company and takes me, who am close to death. That is senseless, so she calls it pitiable, in scorn.
couplets.context: She speaks of the cruelty of the night and grieves.
couplets.speaker: she

links.reason: Night puts all the world to sleep and leaves her as its one companion.

couplets.plain: Crueller even than that cruel one’s cruelty are these nights that now drag on.
couplets.pm: The nights were short in the days of joy with my lover. In these days, when I can’t bear his absence, they are long, and they add their cruelty to his. She calls him cruel because he left without a thought for her pain. His cruelty is delaying his return. The nights have no pity for what that does to her.
couplets.context: She goes on, grieving at the night.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: Crueller even than that cruel one’s cruelty
these nights that now drag on

couplets.plain: If my eyes could go where he is, as my heart does, they wouldn’t be swimming in this flood of water.
couplets.pm: If they could travel quickly to where my lover is, as my heart can, my eyes wouldn’t swim in this flood of their own water. They can’t, so swimming is all that is left to them. The heart travels by thought, but a body must walk, so the eyes can’t go with it and see him. This opens the next chapter.
couplets.context: Her friend says she shouldn’t weep, because her eyes are losing their great beauty. She answers.
couplets.speaker: she

links.quote: swimming in this flood of water
links.reason: Her tears have become a flood that her eyes must swim.

links.quote: If my eyes could go where he is, as my heart does
links.reason: Her eyes are pictured as unable to follow where her heart goes.

ideaLinks.quote: The joy of desire is a sea
ideaLinks.reason: Says in plain words that desire brings joy, and joy as wide as the sea.

ideaLinks.quote: when it turns on you, the pain is greater than that sea
ideaLinks.reason: The desire that gives that joy, once it turns on you, brings pain greater than the joy.
